prompt:
The table below shows the signs of velocity and acceleration for four different particles moving along a horizontal straight line:

Particle P: velocity > 0, acceleration > 0
Particle Q: velocity > 0, acceleration < 0
Particle R: velocity < 0, acceleration > 0
Particle S: velocity < 0, acceleration < 0

Which particle is moving in the negative direction and slowing down?

answer.explanation: Moving in the negative direction requires velocity < 0 (Particles R and S). Slowing down requires acceleration to have the opposite sign to velocity, so acceleration must be > 0. Therefore, Particle R is slowing down while moving in the negative direction.

distractor_explanations: Particle P has velocity > 0 (positive direction) and speeds up (same sign).
Particle Q slows down, but is moving in the positive direction (velocity > 0).
Correct: Particle R has velocity < 0 (negative direction) and acceleration > 0 (opposite sign, so slowing down).
Particle S has velocity < 0 and acceleration < 0; because both signs match, Particle S is speeding up in the negative direction.
hints: The direction of motion is determined solely by the sign of velocity.
An object slows down when velocity and acceleration have opposite signs.
solution: C. Velocity < 0 means moving in the negative direction. Acceleration > 0 opposes velocity, causing speed to decrease.
teacher_walkthrough: Guide students through the two-step logic: first filter by motion direction (velocity < 0 gives R or S).
Next evaluate speed change: same signs mean speeding up, opposite signs mean slowing down.
Velocity < 0 and acceleration > 0 give opposite signs, which means slowing down. Thus R is correct.
